# 0: Load files

First, we load the two csv files.

```{r}

s2 <- read_csv(here("data", "TADA_A1_set2.csv"))
```

# 2: Count total posts

Before counting total posts, we choose to filter out languages other than English. In many languages, "fent" is a common verb, and it will also be easiest to determine context and associations and understand n-grams in English.

```{r}
#| label: filter to english

s1e <- s1 |> filter(language == "English")

s2e <- s2 |> filter(language == "English")

cat("Set 1 English Tweets:", nrow(s1e), "\n")
cat("Set 2 English Tweets:", nrow(s2e), "\n")

se <- bind_rows(s1e |> mutate(set = 1), 
                s2e |> mutate(set = 2))

inds_1 <- 1:nrow(s1e)

inds_2 <- (nrow(s1e) + 1):nrow(se)
```

# 3: Tweets by keyword

Before searching for specific keywords, we create a corpus and preprocess the tweets.

```{r}
#| label: corpus

# Identify text
tweet_text <- se$text |> 
  str_replace_all("\\s+", " ")

# Create corpus
tweet_text_corpus <- VCorpus(VectorSource(tweet_text))

# Collapse white space
tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(stripWhitespace))

# Lowercase
tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(tolower))

# Remove underscores
removeUnderscores <- function(x){
  str_replace_all(x, "_", "")
  }

tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(removeUnderscores))

# Replace any other punctuation and symbols with a space

replacePunctSym <- function(x){
  str_replace_all(x, "[\\p{P}|\\p{S}]", " ")
  }

tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(replacePunctSym))

replaceHighUTFs <- function(x){
  str_replace_all(x, "[^\\x01-\\xE1BFBE]", " ")
  }

tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(replaceHighUTFs))

# Remove numbers (including superscripts and subscripts)
removeAllNumbers <- function(x){
  str_remove_all(x, "[\\p{N}]")
}

tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(removeAllNumbers))

# Remove URLs
removeURLs <- function(x) gsub("http(s)?(\\s)?[[:alnum:]]+", "", x)

tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(removeURLs))

# Remove stop words
my_stops <- c(replacePunctSym(stopwords()),  
              "can", "yes", "yeah", "via", "t", "co")

tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(
  tweet_text_corpus, 
  content_transformer(removeWords),
  words = my_stops
)

# Stem words
tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(
  tweet_text_corpus, 
  content_transformer(stemDocument)
)

# Remove stopwords from stemmed words
tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(
  tweet_text_corpus, 
  content_transformer(removeWords),
  words = my_stops
)

# Collapse white space again
tweet_text_corpus <- tm_map(tweet_text_corpus, 
                            content_transformer(stripWhitespace))

# Make document term matrix
doc_term_mx <- DocumentTermMatrix(tweet_text_corpus,
                                  control = list(tokenize = "Boost"))

doc_term_mx_bin <- DocumentTermMatrix(tweet_text_corpus,
                                      control = list(tokenize = "Boost",
                                                     weighting = weightBin))
```

By looking at the words tokenized in this document term matrix, we find many potential analogs of fentanyl. We look at all words that include "fent" and identify specific instances that we can exclude, like names and other brand names.

```{r}
#| label: fent keyword clarification

dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]][which(str_detect(dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]], "fent"))]

# Identify options to exclude for fentanyl
fent_exc <- c("fentiman", "fentimansltd",
              "fentmaryvonn",
              "fentybeauti", "fentyeffect", "fentyoffici",
              "gracefentiman", 
              "jackfentonnn", "lalisaxfenti", "rakimfenti",
              "savagexfenti")

fent_cols <- which(
  str_detect(dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]], "fent") &
    !(dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]] %in% fent_exc)
)

```

```{r}
#| label: methadone keyword clarification

dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]][which(str_detect(dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]], "metha"))]

# Identify options to include for methadone
# https://www.drugs.com/cons/methadose.html#brand-names
meth_cols <- which(
  str_detect(dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]], 
             "methado|methason|doloph|disket")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: suboxone keyword clarification

dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]][which(str_detect(dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]], "subox"))]

# Identify options to include for suboxone
subox_cols <- which(
  str_detect(dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]], 
             "subox")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: keyword counts

keyword_counts <- tibble(
  keyword = c("methadone", "suboxone", "fentanyl"),
  count_term = c(
    col_sums(doc_term_mx_bin[, "methadon"]),
    col_sums(doc_term_mx_bin[, "suboxon"]),
    col_sums(doc_term_mx_bin[, "fentanyl"])
  ),
  count_all = c(
    sum(col_sums(doc_term_mx_bin[, meth_cols])),
    sum(col_sums(doc_term_mx_bin[, subox_cols])),
    sum(col_sums(doc_term_mx_bin[, fent_cols]))
  )
) |> 
  mutate(pct_term = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 0.01)(count_term / count_all))

kbl(keyword_counts,
    caption = "Tweets by Keyword",
    booktabs = T,
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) |> 
  kable_styling(full_width = F)
```

  - acrylfentanyl
  - alfentanil
  - benzylfentanyl
  - butyrfentanyl
  - carfentanil
  - crotonylfentanyl

  - despropionylfentanyl

  - methoxyacetylyfentanyl
  - methylfentanyl
  - remifentanil
  - sufentanil
  - valerylfentanyl

# 5: Associated Topics

Since each term's correct spelling makes up the vast majority of its appearances, for simplicity we find associations with each term alone. We do not incorporate all of the alternative spellings and associated terms. 

```{r}
#| label: associated topics

# Get vector for each term we are interested in
dtm_vec_meth <- as.vector(doc_term_mx[, "methadon"])
dtm_vec_subox <- as.vector(doc_term_mx[, "suboxon"])
dtm_vec_fent <- as.vector(doc_term_mx[, "fentanyl"])

# Count instances of every word in matrix
word_counts <- col_sums(doc_term_mx)

# Set threshold to keep as 10% of lowest key term frequency
word_thresh <- 0.1 * min(keyword_counts$count_term)

# Filter terms to pass this threshold
candidate_nums <- which(word_counts >= word_thresh)

# Pre-allocate correlation vectors
cor_vec_meth <- cor_vec_subox <- cor_vec_fent <- rep(0, length(candidate_nums))
dtm_vec_col <- dtm_vec_meth * 0

# Calculate correlation between key terms and each candidate term
for(term_num in 1:length(candidate_nums)){
  
  dtm_vec_col[] <- as.vector(doc_term_mx[, term_num])
  
  cor_vec_meth[term_num] <- cor(dtm_vec_meth, dtm_vec_col)
  cor_vec_subox[term_num] <- cor(dtm_vec_subox, dtm_vec_col)
  cor_vec_fent[term_num] <- cor(dtm_vec_fent, dtm_vec_col)
}

# Match these correlations to corresponding words
cor_tbl_meth <- tibble(
  cand_index = which(-cor_vec_meth %in% head(sort(-cor_vec_meth), 10))
) |> 
  mutate(corr = map_dbl(cand_index, \(x) cor_vec_meth[x])) |> 
  mutate(mx_index = map_dbl(cand_index, \(x) candidate_nums[x])) |> 
  mutate(term = map_chr(mx_index, \(x) dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]][x])) |> 
  arrange(desc(corr))

cor_tbl_subox <- tibble(
  cand_index = which(-cor_vec_subox %in% head(sort(-cor_vec_subox), 10))
) |> 
  mutate(corr = map_dbl(cand_index, \(x) cor_vec_subox[x])) |> 
  mutate(mx_index = map_dbl(cand_index, \(x) candidate_nums[x])) |> 
  mutate(term = map_chr(mx_index, \(x) dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]][x])) |> 
  arrange(desc(corr))

cor_tbl_fent <- tibble(
  cand_index = which(-cor_vec_fent %in% head(sort(-cor_vec_fent), 10))
) |> 
  mutate(corr = map_dbl(cand_index, \(x) cor_vec_fent[x])) |> 
  mutate(mx_index = map_dbl(cand_index, \(x) candidate_nums[x])) |> 
  mutate(term = map_chr(mx_index, \(x) dimnames(doc_term_mx)[[2]][x])) |> 
  arrange(desc(corr))
```

# 8: Bigrams

```{r}
#| label: create bigrams

# Find single-word tweets
words_per_text <- map_dbl(
  tweet_text_corpus$content,
  function(x){
    length(unlist(strsplit(x$content, split = " ")))
  }
)

# Identify which tweets need to be removed for bigrams
inds_too_short <- which(words_per_text < 2)

# Count which tweets need to be removed in each set
num_too_short_1 <- sum(inds_too_short <= nrow(s1e))

# Create new corpus for bigrams
text_corpus_bi <- tweet_text_corpus[which(words_per_text >= 2)]

# Correct indices for 2 sets in this corpus
inds_bi_1 <- 1:(nrow(s1e) - num_too_short_1)
inds_bi_2 <- (max(inds_bi_1) + 1):length(text_corpus_bi)

# temp_list <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(text_corpus_bi))
# for(t_i in 1:length(text_corpus_bi)){
#   temp_list[[t_i]] <- ngramrr(text_corpus_bi$content[[t_i]]$content,
#                               ngmin = 2, ngmax = 2)
# }

# Make document term matrix
dtm_bi <- dtm2(
  text_corpus_bi,
  ngmin = 2, ngmax = 2
)
```

```{r}
#| label: count most frequent terms

bigram_freqs_1 <- col_sums(dtm_bi[inds_bi_1,])

bigram_freqs_2 <- col_sums(dtm_bi[inds_bi_2,])

top10_1 <- sort(bigram_freqs_1, decreasing = T)[1:10]

top10_2 <- sort(bigram_freqs_2, decreasing = T)[1:10]
  
tbl10_1 <- enframe(top10_1, name = "Term", value = "Frequency")

tbl10_2 <- enframe(top10_2, name = "Term", value = "Frequency")

top10_bis <- tibble(
  "Term" = unique(c(tbl10_1$Term, tbl10_2$Term))
) |> 
  mutate(
    count_1 = map_dbl(Term, \(x) col_sums(dtm_bi[inds_bi_1, x])),
    count_2 = map_dbl(Term, \(x) col_sums(dtm_bi[inds_bi_2, x]))
  ) |> 
  mutate(total = count_1 + count_2) |> 
  mutate(count_per_doc_1 = count_1 / length(inds_bi_1),
         count_per_doc_2 = count_2 / length(inds_bi_2),
         count_per_doc_total = total / length(text_corpus_bi)) |> 
  arrange(desc(total))

```
